method: Each of three fresh Miniflare runtimes seeded 128 and 1,024 unique keys into hash-bucket Durable Objects at 8/16/32/64/128 buckets per key set. The runtime was disposed and recreated over the same SQLite state before 128-concurrency unique-key read waves. Every read checked exact key/value/revision 1. No retries.
interpretation: The benchmark-only bucketed append-only owner design served 1,024 independent keys using 64 buckets with p99 46/56/53 ms across three local runtime-restart trials at 128 concurrent requests. All 17,280 reads completed exactly and all seed writes were acknowledged. At one bucket per key, the 1,024-key layout was unstable: p99 91/93/148 ms. This suggests bounded grouping can avoid both one-hot-owner contention and a large cold-actor activation wave for the tested workload; it is not a production SLO or infinite-capacity proof.
limitations: Local Miniflare/SQLite, closed-loop 128-concurrency waves, three trials on one machine.
No open-loop traffic, sustained windows, mixed cross-key writes, failure injection, Cloudflare placement or external caller latency.
Append-only facts and linearizability are scoped to one key within one bucket. There is no atomic transaction or snapshot across buckets, and the prototype does not implement Poneglyph Datalog joins.
This tests up to 1,024 keys, not unbounded growth; actor count, storage size, hot-bucket contention and eviction behavior require further capacity testing.
